title: Thiol-free reducing agents in electrophoretic separations and FASP proteolytic digestions for the analysis of metal-binding proteins
author: Moraleja, Moreno-Gordaliza, et al.
materials: 1.For subsequent SDS-PAGE separation, add 200 μL LSB to the preconcentrated cytosolic fraction (the retentate fraction from step 11 (Sample preparation procedure)) and vortex.2.Heat at 95 °C for 1 min in a thermoblock.3.Allow to cool down the sample, and once at room temperature (RT), add TCEP to a final concentration of 50 mM. In comparison to the conventional SDS-PAGE method [3], the heating time was shortened to 1 min and the reductant was added at a lower temperature (RT instead of 95 °C).▴Critical step: avoid boiling samples with the reductant in order to preserve the integrity of the metal–protein complexes.4.Load the sample (a total protein content of 50 μg) into the gel wells. Start electrophoresis at constant current (12 mA per gel until samples were stacked an then the current was increased to 20 mA per gel until the end of the separation).5.Wash the gels with Milli-Q grade water for 20 min and incubate the gel in the fixing solution for 1 h in an oscillating shaker.6.Stain the gel with colloidal Coomassie Blue for 1 h.7.Wash the gel twice with 20 mL of Milli-Q grade water for 1 h per wash.8.Excise protein bands from the gels with a scalpel.9.Wash the gel slices for at least 1 h in 500 μL of 50 mM NH4HCO3. Discard the wash.10.Wash the gel slices in 500 μL of 50% acetonitrile/50 mM NH4HCO3 with shaking for 1 h. Discard the wash. Cut the gel band into 1 mm2 pieces and transfer to a 500 μL Protein Lo-Bind tube (Eppendorf).▴Critical step: Make sure that the gel slices stay wet with the wash solution to facilitate cutting and transfer.11.Add 50 μL of acetonitrile to shrink the gel pieces. After 10–15 min, remove the solvent and dry the gel slices in a centrifugal evaporator.12.Re-swell the gel pieces with 50 mM NH4HCO3 containing 12.5 ng/μL of trypsin and keep them in ice during reswelling (as required, typically add 10–20 μL). Once the gels have completely re-swollen, add 50 mM NH4HCO3 to cover the gel pieces (around 10–20 μL). Cap the tubes tightly and cover with parafilm to avoid evaporation. Incubate at 37 °C overnight (∼16 h) with gentle agitation using a thermomixer at 300 r.p.m.▴Critical step: gel pieces need to stay wet during the digestion.13.After completing the digestion, collect supernatants and transfer them to a Lo-Bind Eppendorf, keeping them at 4 °C. Next, extract the peptides remaining in the gel with 30 μL of 2% formic acid by vortexing, and incubate for 30 min at RT. Pool the extracted peptides with the original supernatant.14.Finally, add 30 μL of a solution containing 50% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid, and incubate for another 30 min at RT. Pool the extraction solution with the previous ones, and evaporate samples in a vacuum centrifuge to dryness. Store the dry peptides at −80 °C until required, within a few months.15.For protein identification, analysis by nLC–ESI-LTQ-MS/MS (or a similar LC–MS/MS platform) is proposed. Resuspend the dried peptides in 10 μL of buffer A and sonicate for 10 min in an ultrasonic bath. Then start the analysis as follows: Inject aliquots of 5 μL, using a 20 μL loop and a pick-up method, and load on a trap-column at a 3 μL min−1 flow rate using buffer A as mobile phase. Reverse the flow at 200 nL min−1 to elute and transfer the preconcentrated peptides to a reverse phase microcapillary analytical column. Elute peptides applying a three-step gradient: 5–15% B linear for 5 min, 15–40% B linear for 40 min and 40–80% B linear for another 15 min, holding the system at 80% B for 10 min. The end of the column was connected to a stainless steel nano-bore emitter for spraying and coupling with the LTQ. The spray voltage was set at 1.70 kV. Peptides were scanned and fragmented using a triple play scan method, consisting on acquisition of full enhanced MS scans in the positive ion mode, over the m/z range 400–1600, followed by zoom scans and further full enhanced MS/MS, acquired in profile mode, of the three most intense peaks in the full MS scan. CID activation of ions was applied in MS/MS experiments, with 35% relative collision energy and 30 ms activation time, being isolation width of the precursor ions set to 4. Dynamic exclusion was enabled with a repeat count of 1, using a 180 s exclusion duration window. For data analysis, spectra were assessed with the Xcalibur Qual Browser software (Thermo Scientific). MS/MS spectra search on NCBI protein databases using SEQUEST and MASCOT allowed the identification of proteins. The search was performed against a rat (Rattus norvegicus) NCBI database.

steps.title: Mince kidney tissue on ice
steps.instruction: Place ~0.250 g rat kidney tissue (treated with a metal‑based chemotherapeutic) in a Petri dish on ice and mince with a scalpel.

steps.title: Add buffer and protease inhibitor
steps.instruction: Transfer minced tissue to a tube, add 3 mL pre‑chilled buffer and 12.5 µL protease‑inhibitor cocktail, keep the tube on ice for all subsequent steps (2–4).

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize for at least 15 min using a tight‑fitting Teflon pestle attached to a power drill set >1000 rpm, stroking slowly (15 s per stroke, 30 s per up‑down cycle).

steps.title: Inspect and re‑homogenize if needed
steps.instruction: If intact tissue remains, re‑homogenize for an additional 1 min. Wear safety glasses and a face shield to avoid glass breakage.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate
steps.instruction: Decant homogenate into a pre‑cooled centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 40 min in a pre‑cooled rotor (4 °C).

steps.title: Collect cytosolic supernatant
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant, keep it on an ice‑bath (all steps at 4 °C). The supernatant may be frozen at –80 °C for later use.

steps.title: Filter and load onto SEC column
steps.instruction: Inject the cytosolic fraction through a 0.22 µm PVDF filter directly onto the size‑exclusion chromatography (SEC) column.

steps.title: Collect SEC fractions
steps.instruction: Collect 0.8 mL fractions every minute from the SEC column.

steps.title: Determine Pt and protein content
steps.instruction: Measure Pt in each fraction by ICP‑MS (monitor 195Pt, 10 channels/AMU, 0.6 ms integration) and protein by Bradford assay.

steps.title: Select high‑Pt/protein fractions
steps.instruction: Identify fractions with the highest Pt‑to‑protein ratio for further analysis.

steps.title: Ultrafiltration of selected fractions
steps.instruction: Pool ten identical high‑ratio fractions and ultrafilter through an Amicon Ultra‑4 mL 3 kDa cut‑off filter; collect the retentate.

steps.title: Add LSB to retentate (SDS‑PAGE)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL LDS sample buffer (LSB) to the retentate and vortex.

steps.title: Heat sample briefly
steps.instruction: Heat at 95 °C for 1 min in a thermoblock.

steps.title: Add TCEP reductant
steps.instruction: Cool to room temperature, then add TCEP to a final concentration of 50 mM (avoid boiling with reductant).

steps.title: Load gel and run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load 50 µg total protein per well, run at constant 12 mA until stacking is complete, then increase to 20 mA until the end of separation.

steps.title: Wash and fix gel
steps.instruction: Wash gels with Milli‑Q water for 20 min, then incubate in fixing solution for 1 h on an oscillating shaker.

steps.title: Stain gel with Coomassie
steps.instruction: Stain the gel with colloidal Coomassie Blue for 1 h.

steps.title: Wash stained gel
steps.instruction: Wash the gel twice with 20 mL Milli‑Q water, 1 h per wash.

steps.title: Excise protein bands
steps.instruction: Excise desired protein bands from the gel using a scalpel.

steps.title: Initial gel slice wash
steps.instruction: Wash gel slices for ≥1 h in 500 µL 50 mM NH₄HCO₃; discard the wash.

steps.title: Second gel slice wash
steps.instruction: Wash gel slices for 1 h in 500 µL 50 % acetonitrile / 50 mM NH₄HCO₃ with shaking; discard the wash.

steps.title: Cut gel pieces and transfer
steps.instruction: Cut each gel band into ~1 mm² pieces and transfer to a 500 µL Protein Lo‑Bind tube; keep pieces wet.

steps.title: Shrink gel pieces with ACN
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL acetonitrile, incubate 10–15 min, remove solvent, then dry the pieces in a centrifugal evaporator.

steps.title: Re‑swell gel pieces with trypsin
steps.instruction: Add 50 mM NH₄HCO₃ containing 12.5 ng/µL trypsin (10–20 µL) on ice, then add additional 50 mM NH₄HCO₃ (10–20 µL) to cover; cap, seal with parafilm, incubate at 37 °C overnight (~16 h) with gentle agitation (300 rpm).

steps.title: Collect digestion supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer supernatant to a Lo‑Bind tube, keep at 4 °C.

steps.title: Extract remaining peptides with FA
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL 2 % formic acid, vortex, incubate 30 min at RT; pool with the previous supernatant.

steps.title: Final peptide extraction
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL 50 % acetonitrile / 0.1 % formic acid, incubate 30 min at RT; pool, evaporate to dryness in a vacuum centrifuge, store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend peptides for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Resuspend dried peptides in 10 µL buffer A, sonicate 10 min in an ultrasonic bath.

steps.title: Inject peptides into LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Inject 5 µL (20 µL loop, pick‑up mode) onto a trap column at 3 µL min⁻¹ (buffer A). Reverse flow at 200 nL min⁻¹ to the analytical column.

steps.title: Apply LC gradient
steps.instruction: Run a three‑step gradient: 5–15 % B linear 5 min, 15–40 % B linear 40 min, 40–80 % B linear 15 min, hold at 80 % B for 10 min.

steps.title: Set MS acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Spray voltage 1.70 kV; acquire full MS scans (m/z 400–1600, positive mode), then zoom scans and MS/MS of the three most intense peaks. CID 35 % CE, 30 ms activation, isolation width 4 m/z. Dynamic exclusion: repeat count 1, exclusion duration 180 s.

steps.title: Analyze data
steps.instruction: Process spectra with Xcalibur Qual Browser; search MS/MS spectra against the Rat (Rattus norvegicus) NCBI database using SEQUEST and MASCOT.

steps.title: Prepare OFFGEL focusing buffer
steps.instruction: Add 2.88 mL focusing buffer and 0.72 mL Milli‑Q water (final 3.6 mL) to the retentate, vortex. Do NOT add thiourea.

steps.title: Rehydrate IPG strip
steps.instruction: Place a pH 3–10 IPG strip in the OFFGEL tray and rehydrate with 40 µL rehydration buffer per manufacturer’s instructions; avoid touching the strip.

steps.title: Load sample into OFFGEL wells
steps.instruction: Load 150 µL of the prepared sample into each well of the OFFGEL device.

steps.title: Run OFFGEL fractionation
steps.instruction: Focus at 20 °C, max current 50 µA, voltage 500–4000 V until 50 kV·h⁻¹ is reached (≈24 h).

steps.title: Collect OFFGEL fractions
steps.instruction: Aspirate liquid from each well, transfer 100–150 µL fractions to 500 µL Lo‑Bind tubes; freeze at –80 °C if needed.

steps.title: Load OFFGEL fraction onto spin filter
steps.instruction: Load 100 µL OFFGEL fraction (≈250 µg protein) into a Vivacon spin filter.

steps.title: Urea wash step 1
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL UA solution, centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min at 25 °C, discard filtrate. Repeat once.

steps.title: TBP reduction step
steps.instruction: Dilute retentate 1:1 with 10 mM TBP to reach 5 mM TBP, incubate 30 min RT, centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min RT, discard filtrate.

steps.title: IAA alkylation step
steps.instruction: Add IAA to 20 mM final, incubate 30 min RT in the dark, centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min RT, discard filtrate.

steps.title: Urea buffer clean‑up
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL UB solution, centrifuge; repeat twice; discard filtrates each time.

steps.title: First trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Add 5 µg trypsin in 100 µL UB, incubate 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Collect first peptide eluate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min RT, collect filtrate (peptides).

steps.title: Wash filter after first digestion
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL UB, centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min RT; repeat three times, pooling all filtrates with the first peptide eluate.

steps.title: Second trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Add 5 µg fresh trypsin to the retentate, incubate 37 °C (time as for first digestion).

steps.title: Collect second peptide eluate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min RT, collect filtrate.

steps.title: Wash filter after second digestion
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL UB, centrifuge 14 000 × g 15 min RT; repeat three times, pool all filtrates (final volume ~250–300 µL).

steps.title: Desalt and concentrate peptides
steps.instruction: Perform micro‑SPE using OMIX C18 tips (100 µL); elute peptides in 50 µL 70 % acetonitrile / 0.1 % formic acid.

steps.title: Dry and reconstitute for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Evaporate eluates to dryness, reconstitute in 10 µL buffer A, then analyse by nLC‑ESI‑LTQ‑MS/MS as described in steps 27–31.

description: Two protocols are detailed for the analysis of metal–protein complexes in biological samples, based on methods recently demonstrated for kidney cytosolic proteins from rats treated with platinum-based chemotherapeutic drugs. The described procedures include either TCEP-based rSDS-PAGE [1], or TBP-based rOFFGEL-IEF in combination with a FASP tryptic digestion [2], followed by identification by nLC–ESI-LTQ-MS/MS. Prior to both protocols, a sample preparation step should be performed in order to obtain cytosolic protein fractions with the highest Pt to protein ratio from the metallodrug-exposed kidney by size exclusion chromatography (SEC)-ICP-MS.
